title: Cross-Border Data Segmentation & Access Controls Annex
content:
Purpose
This annex supplements the master services agreement (MSA) or data processing agreement (DPA) between the Parties and defines additional controls and contractual commitments applicable when Vendor processes Customer data that may traverse or be stored outside the Customer’s primary jurisdictions. The goal is to minimize cross-border exposure and ensure segmented access and inspection rights where local regulations or Customer policy require geographic separation.

Scope
This Annex applies to: (a) Personal Data, Confidential Information, and Customer Content processed by Vendor; and (b) any Subprocessor engaged by Vendor that performs processing which may result in data transfer across national borders. This Annex does not replace the core DPA; it augments it and, where there is a conflict, the stricter control shall govern.

Definitions
- Data Segmentation: Logical and/or physical separation of data elements such that Customer data subject to a given jurisdiction is stored, indexed, and accessed in separate compute/storage partitions.
- Regional Processing Location: The geographic region or country where processing or storage takes place.
- Data Residency Commitment: A contractual promise by Vendor to keep specific categories of data within one or more specified jurisdictions.
- Local Access Gate: Controls that prevent access to segmented data from outside an approved region (network-level, identity-bound, or policy-based controls).

1. Data Residency and Segmentation
1.1 Residency Commitments. Vendor shall provide the Customer with the ability to designate, by data class or tenant identifier, the Region(s) in which Customer Content will be stored at rest and processed. Where Customer designates a Residency Commitment for a data class, Vendor shall not store or process that data outside the designated Region(s) except as allowed under Section 1.3.
1.2 Logical & Physical Segmentation. Vendor shall implement segmentation controls sufficient to ensure that data governed by a Residency Commitment is logically separated from other Customers’ data, and where technically feasible, stored on infrastructure (logical clusters or physical hosts) constrained to the designated Region.
1.3 Permitted Exceptions. Vendor may transfer or process segmented data outside the designated Region only (a) to comply with a binding legal obligation, (b) with Customer’s prior written consent, or (c) to restore service after an outage in the designated Region, where Vendor documents the business justification and notifies Customer within 48 hours.

2. Cross-border Transfer Mechanisms and Legal Basis
2.1 Transfer Mechanisms. For transfers outside the European Economic Area, United Kingdom, or other jurisdictions with data export controls, Vendor shall rely on published, accepted transfer mechanisms (e.g., Standard Contractual Clauses, adequacy decisions) or another lawful basis documented in a Transfer Impact Assessment provided to Customer upon request.
2.2 Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA). Prior to initiating transfers that materially change the processing risk profile (new Region, new Subprocessor, different legal regime), Vendor shall produce a TIA describing legal risks, technical mitigations (encryption, split-processing, pseudonymization), and expected retention windows. The TIA shall be delivered to Customer and trigger a review meeting if Customer objects within 10 business days.

3. Access Controls and Local Access Gates
3.1 Region-Bound Access. Vendor shall enforce Region-bound access policies for operational and engineering personnel. Access to segmented datasets shall be restricted such that personnel working from outside the designated Region cannot access the data unless subject to an approved exception (see 3.4).
3.2 Identity & Privileged Access Management. Vendor must use strong, federated identity (SAML/OIDC), multi-factor authentication, least-privilege role definitions, and just-in-time elevation for administrative access to segmented data. All privileged sessions that access segmented data must be logged and retained for a minimum of 12 months.
3.3 Network Controls. Vendor shall use network-level controls (VPC/VNet isolation, regional egress policies, private interconnects) to prevent unauthorized cross-region network access to segmented storage and runtime systems.
3.4 Temporary Access Exceptions. Temporary cross-region access is permitted only for documented operational reasons, subject to Customer approval where the access involves Personal Data. Vendor shall create an access exception ticket, describe the scope and duration, apply compensating controls (audit + session recording + scoped role), and automatically revoke access at the exception expiration.

4. Subprocessors, Onboarding, and Local Reviews
4.1 Subprocessor Segmentation Requirements. Vendor shall require Subprocessors to honor Customer Residency Commitments and implement equivalent segmentation and access controls. Vendor’s Subprocessor agreements shall include specific contractual obligations mirroring Sections 1–3 and shall permit Customer’s audit rights as set forth below.
4.2 Subprocessor Onboarding Controls. Prior to adding a new Subprocessor that will handle segmented data, Vendor shall notify Customer (30 days prior for new Subprocessors; 7 days for emergency replacements) with the Subprocessor name, location, processing activities, and a summary of segmentation controls.

5. Encryption & Key Management
5.1 Data at Rest & In Transit. Vendor shall encrypt Customer Content at rest and in transit using industry-standard algorithms (AES-256 or equivalent for at-rest; TLS 1.2+ for in-transit).
5.2 Customer-Controlled Keys. For Customers requiring enhanced residency assurances, Vendor offers optional customer-managed keys (CMK) or dedicated KMS partitions such that cryptographic keys for segmented data are stored within the same jurisdictional boundaries, where technically supported.
5.3 Key Escrow & Access. Where Vendor manages keys, Vendor shall limit key access to a small set of personnel under documented key-access policies, require MFA, and log and retain key usage records for at least 12 months.

6. Monitoring, Logging & Auditability
6.1 Regional Audit Trails. Vendor shall maintain region-specific audit logs that record: administrative actions, data access events, key usage, and cross-region replication actions. Logs for segmented data must be stored with a tag identifying residency and retained per Customer’s retention policy, minimum 12 months.
6.2 Audit Rights. Customer or a mutually agreed third-party auditor may, upon reasonable notice and subject to confidentiality protections, conduct an audit focused on segmented data controls, Subprocessor compliance, and access controls. Audit frequency: no more than once per 12 months unless a material incident occurs.

7. Incident Response & Notification
7.1 Region-Specific Incident Handling. Vendor shall classify incidents by affected Region(s) and provide region-specific incident response playbooks. If a data incident involves segmented data or a cross-border exposure, Vendor shall notify Customer within 24 hours of detection and provide a remedial timeline.
7.2 Forensics & Preservation. Vendor shall preserve all logs and forensic artifacts related to the incident for the purposes of investigation and shall cooperate with Customer’s incident response team and legal counsel as reasonably requested.

8. Data Localization & Decommissioning
8.1 Localized Deletion & Data Purge. Vendor shall offer APIs or deletion procedures to permanently remove segmented data within the designated Region(s). Upon termination of services or at Customer’s direction, Vendor shall delete segmented data and provide a deletion certificate describing the assets wiped and timestamps.
8.2 Replication & Backup Constraints. Backups containing segmented data shall adhere to Residency Commitments. Vendor shall document backup locations and retention windows and shall honor Customer requests to keep backups within specified Regions.

9. Representations, Warranty & Liability
9.1 Representations. Vendor represents that: (a) it will implement and maintain the technical and organizational measures described in this Annex; (b) Subprocessors will be contractually bound to materially equivalent obligations; and (c) it will comply with applicable export controls and cross-border data transfer laws.
9.2 Limitations. Parties acknowledge that certain lawful process requirements (subpoenas, governmental orders) may compel access. Vendor shall, when permitted, challenge such requests and notify Customer unless legally prohibited.
9.3 Liability. Vendor’s liability for breaches of the Residency Commitments and segmentation controls resulting from Vendor’s negligence or willful misconduct shall be addressed in the liability section of the MSA/DPA; absent wilful misconduct, the Parties agree to follow the contractual cap and remedies agreed in the MSA.

10. Change Control & Enhancements
10.1 Material Changes. Vendor will provide at least 60 days’ notice prior to any material change to infrastructure, hosting regions, or segmentation architecture that could affect Residency Commitments.
10.2 Non-Material Updates. Security patching, routine upgrades, and minor infra changes that do not change the residency profile will be documented in the next quarterly security bulletin.

11. Execution & Scope of Annex
This Annex is incorporated into and made part of the MSA/DPA between Customer and Vendor as of the Effective Date. In case of conflict, the more protective provision for Personal Data shall prevail.

Notes for Negotiation (internal):
- Consider offering regionalized pricing for data residency zones that require dedicated infrastructure.
- Be prepared to offer CMK (customer-managed keys) or bring-your-own-key in high-risk jurisdictions.
- Clarify what counts as a "material change" to avoid scope creep on notices.
- Maintain a templated TIA to speed reviews for repeat customers.
